selection.rationale: Measured evidence on this exact revision (8c0ae97, clean baseline latency_ms 4.224596): the single forward runs 88 CUDA kernels whose active union is 4068.35us inside the 4.22ms synchronized window (kernel span 4145.1us, gaps only 76.79us), so the window is ~96% GPU-busy and launch-overhead-only fixes cap at ~1.8%. Kernel-time split (leaf, non-overlapping): conv2d 3035.6us (73.3%), batch_norm 427.1us (10.3%), relu 342.8us (8.3%), max_pool 199.3us (4.8%), add_ 121.1us (2.9%). The convs execute at ~19 TFLOP/s FP32 (~58 GFLOP / 3.04ms), i.e. at the Ampere FP32 roofline (scudnn/winograd kernels already chosen by heuristics) and TF32 is banned by the frozen numerical policy, so conv time has no legal headroom; the slack is the memory-bound pointwise chain. BatchNorm in eval is a pure per-channel affine (cudnn bn_fw_inf_1C11 kernels, 427.1us) that folds exactly into conv weight/bias; the 8 residual add_+ReLU pairs (121.1us + same-size relu fraction of 342.8us) can run as one fused pointwise kernel per basic layer; the 76.8us of inter-kernel gaps can additionally be reclaimed by CUDA-graph capture of the static single-stream sequence. All of these edits lie inside one coherent editable boundary: the forward of ResNetForImageClassification (group eca3643289778aea5af3, target 'model', one call f2cf62caf57ad09f5d2f36aa owning all 88 kernels and the whole module subtree). Replacing this whole bundle (rather than editing leaf conv/BN groups) is required so the inherited aten::batch_norm/add_/relu calls that the rewrite legitimately eliminates are explicitly excused by whole-bundle replacement instead of silently losing coverage; the replacement itself is invoked through the Python boundary on every run and must return the full [32,1000] logits computed on the current GPU-resident input.
selection.hypothesis: Replacing ResNetForImageClassification.forward with a whole-bundle fused inference implementation reduces latency_ms from 4.224596 by roughly 12-16% (hypothesis ~3.55-3.75ms), tested by the framework's clean timing. The implementation: (1) at build time, fold every eval BatchNorm2d's affine (gamma/sqrt(var+eps), beta, running stats) into the preceding conv's weight and a new bias - mathematically identical, removing all 20 bn_fw_inf_1C11 kernels (427.1us, 10.3% of kernel time); (2) keep conv2d/maxpool/adaptive_avg_pool2d/linear calls numerically identical under the frozen FP32/no-TF32/cudnn.benchmark=False policy (convs are at the FP32 roofline and are not targeted); (3) fuse each residual add+ReLU into a single pointwise kernel (halves that tensor's memory round-trips, est. ~90-100us); (4) optionally, as a guarded second step, capture the static sequence into a CUDA graph during a legitimate first invocation inside the adapter's actual forward/inference_mode context (binding-contract compliant: replay on current inputs each invocation) to reclaim up to 76.8us of launch gaps. Quality risk is limited to FP32 rounding shifts (BN reorder ~1e-6..1e-5), expected to pass logits atol=rtol=1e-4, exact top1 and the negative control; measured acceptance, not prediction, decides. Convs, workload, batch, precision, measurement boundaries and quality checks are untouched.

proposal.rationale: Whole-bundle replacement of the ResNetForImageClassification forward (module call f2cf62caf57ad09f5d2f36aa, group eca3643289778aea5af3, the single call owning all 88 kernels and the whole module subtree). Measured evidence on this revision (8c0ae97, clean baseline latency_ms 4.224596): the synchronized 4.22ms window is ~96% GPU-busy (kernel union 4068.35us, gaps 76.79us); conv2d 3035.6us (73.3%) already runs at ~19 TFLOP/s FP32 roofline with TF32 banned, so convs are kept as the identical aten::conv2d ops (same shapes, bias-free) with cudnn.benchmark untouched. The optimization targets the memory-bound pointwise chain: (1) every eval BatchNorm2d affine (20 bn_fw_inf_1C11 kernels, 427.1us) is folded at build time into conv weight scale and a per-channel bias - exact algebra, FP32 reassociation only; (2) the 8 residual add_ (121.1us) plus their adjacent ReLU passes run as one fused Triton add+bias+ReLU kernel per basic layer (3 memory accesses per element instead of bn 2 + add 3 + relu 2 = 7; the shortcut conv's folded bias is pre-added into the same kernel's channel bias), and stem/conv1 bias+ReLU run as one fused pass instead of bn+relu (2 instead of 4 accesses); (3) the remaining 76.8us of launch gaps are reclaimed by lazily capturing the static kernel sequence into a CUDA graph on the first CUDA invocation (side-stream warmup, then capture, then a replay-vs-eager verification at 1e-4) and replaying it on subsequent invocations whose input signature (shape/stride/dtype/device/data_ptr) matches the live GPU-resident pixels storage; replay reads the current bytes of that storage, so the workload executes on current inputs every invocation, and any other signature (held-out batch=7, online batch=1, non-contiguous layouts) takes the fully general eager fused path. labels, output_hidden_states, return_dict=False or unknown kwargs fall back to the parent bound forward and are reported via record_route labels (setup_failure:*, parent_fallback_unsupported_signature, eager_fused, captured, cuda_graph_replay, capture_failed, graph_replay_failed). No previous feedback or previous-candidate inputs exist for this task. Expected effect: remove most of the ~0.9ms non-conv pointwise+gap time (BN fold ~0.43ms, fused add/relu ~0.1ms, launch gaps ~0.07ms), i.e. latency_ms ~3.6-3.7ms (-12..15%); measured acceptance decides. CPU FP32 verification of the exact fold/forward composition against the parent module gives max|delta logits| 7.6e-6 on scale-20 logits with exact top1 on the 32-image fixture batch, batch 7 and batch 32 random inputs. Batch, sampling, data, precision policy, measurement boundaries and thresholds are untouched. eliminated_calls lists all 350 descendant calls of the replaced bundle: the 20 aten.batch_norm, 8 aten.add_ and 17 aten.relu parent calls no longer execute because BN is folded and pointwise work runs inside the fused Triton kernels; the aten.conv2d/max_pool2d/adaptive_avg_pool2d/linear/flatten work continues as the same aten ops inside the replacement and will be recaptured by the framework as new calls; the 163 profiler._record_function* entries are collector instrumentation, not project work. Their consumers remain valid because the replacement returns the parent's exact ImageClassifierOutputWithNoAttention structure whose logits are the only product consumed by adapter.observe/close_check/argmax checks.

setup_work.parameter_transform: At build time (no_grad, inference_mode(False) so tensors stay usable in any later context): fold the 20 eval BatchNorm2d affines (gamma/sqrt(var+eps), beta-mean*scale) into contiguous FP32 conv-weight copies (~44.7MB, conv weights stay bias-free so cudnn heuristics see identical shapes) plus per-channel biases, pre-add the shortcut bias into each basic layer's fused bias, and clone the detached classifier weight/bias (~2.1MB). Original parameters are untouched, so parent fallback and framework restore keep exact parent semantics.
setup_work.first_cuda_invocation: Triton JIT compile of the two pointwise kernels, side-stream warmup, CUDA graph capture of the static sequence, and a replay-vs-eager output verification before the graph is used. This happens on the first candidate CUDA call, which precedes the timed repeats (warmup=2, quality checks first); later timed invocations replay.
setup_work.memory: Setup allocates ~46.8MB of folded/cloned FP32 parameters that stay alive for the warm-model lifecycle. The CUDA graph retains a private pool roughly the size of the activation high-water mark, which increases reserved/lifecycle_reserved bytes. Because transient activations move into the graph pool, the per-run peak_allocated_bytes counter is expected to drop while replaying; this is an allocator-scope effect, not a physical-memory saving, and is reported as such. None of these counters measures the graph pool's reserved bytes as allocated.

quality_risks: FP32 reassociation from BN folding and the fused (a+b)+bias add order shifts logits by ~1e-6..1e-5 (CPU FP32 measurement: max 7.6e-6 on scale-20 logits), within atol=rtol=1e-4; exact top1 can only flip if two classes are nearly tied in the reference.
Triton maximum(x, 0) differs from aten clamp in NaN propagation; the frozen fixture and weights are finite, so no NaN is expected on this path.

CUDA graph capture or replay can fail on unusual worker states; every graph step is guarded (capture_failed, capture_verification_failed, graph_replay_failed route labels) and degrades to the general eager fused path, never to wrong output. The graph reads the live input storage, so mutated input contents are recomputed on each replay; different tensor objects with non-matching signatures take the eager path.

Graph replay does not re-execute the parent's inner Python calls; the whole bundle is explicitly replaced and eliminated_calls lists every descendant, with equivalent conv/pool/linear work continuing inside the replacement.

If the evaluator rebuilds the input tensor per invocation (different data_ptr each call), the graph guard routes every call to the eager fused path: still correct, with the BN-fold and fused pointwise savings only.

usage.scope: Observed assistant message snapshots; provider estimates, not invoice
Observed assistant message snapshots; provider estimates, not invoice

external_invariants: FP32 everywhere: weights loaded with dtype=torch.float32 and compute kept in FP32; torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32=False, torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32=False, torch.set_float32_matmul_precision('highest'), torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark=False.
Deterministic seed policy from common.configure(): torch.manual_seed(20261020), 4 CPU threads, 1 inter-op thread.

Model identity and mode unchanged: ResNetForImageClassification initialized from the frozen request assets dir (local_files_only=True, microsoft/resnet-18 weights, num_params=11689512) and kept in eval() on context['device'].

Input construction is frozen: pixels.npy (3 preprocessed FP32 NCHW 224x224 real images) extended to the workload batch via arange(batch) % 3 then .contiguous(), transferred to GPU once outside timing.

Work amount is one full batch forward per measured invocation with no internal iteration, no caching between repeats, and no change to batch (32), architecture, precision, data or output requirements.

Outputs are the full [batch,1000] logits and argmax class ids; quality requires require_exact_top1 (torch.equal on argmax over all 1000 classes) plus torch.testing.assert_close at logits_atol=logits_rtol=1e-4, and the source's negative control must reject a +1 corruption of the reference.

Metric semantics preserved: latency_ms is the wall time of the single synchronized forward; images_per_second = batch*1000/latency_ms is the reciprocal of the same boundary; peak_allocated_bytes is torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() for the measured invocation.

The offline workload row is preserved verbatim, including the memory goal's images_per_second_min_baseline_ratio 0.95 guard, which is scoped to the memory goal and not to the latency objective (which carries no constraints).
